slot.brief: Given z in a form requiring algebraic manipulation (e.g. (1+i)/(1−i) raised to a power), find the modulus and principal argument of the result.

stem: For $w=\left(\dfrac{1+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)^4$, write $w$ in polar form using its principal argument.

verdicts.working: The quotient has modulus 1/√2 and argument 5π/12. Raising to the fourth power gives modulus 1/4 and argument 5π/3, whose principal value is −π/3.

working:
$\left|\dfrac{1+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right|=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$
$\arg\left(\dfrac{1+i}{\sqrt{3}-i}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$
$|w|=\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{4}$
$\arg(w)=4\cdot\dfrac{5\pi}{12}=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\equiv-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\pmod{2\pi}$

Independent check: The quotient has modulus 1/√2 and argument 5π/12. Raising to the fourth power gives modulus 1/4 and argument 5π/3, whose principal value is −π/3.
solution:
Using $|z_1/z_2|=|z_1|/|z_2|$ and $arg(z_1/z_2)=arg z_1-arg z_2$,
$$\left|\frac{1+i}{\sqrt3-i}\right|=\frac1{\sqrt2},\qquad \arg\left(\frac{1+i}{\sqrt3-i}\right)=\frac{5\pi}{12}.$$
Thus $|w|=(1/\sqrt2)^4=1/4$ and $\arg w=4(5\pi/12)=5\pi/3$, whose principal value is $-\pi/3$.
Hence $w=\dfrac14\operatorname{cis}(-\pi/3)$.‏
